identity: Official Arduino CLI Go module source archive, including its separate i18n maintenance CLI.

provenance.verification: Forager recovered a byte-identical proxy.golang.org archive and verified its module checksum against sum.golang.org.
provenance.queue_claim: The flagged function is byte-identical in 0.18.0; scanning that earlier file with the original local rules also produces the wipe false positive. The stated clean-earlier-release premise is not reproduced by this control.

execution_trace: i18n/cmd/main.go -> commands.Execute -> transifex.Command -> pullTransifexCommand.Run -> pullCatalog; this is an explicit maintenance command, not a package import payload.
PersistentPreRun reads TRANSIFEX_PROJECT, TRANSIFEX_RESOURCE and TRANSIFEX_API_KEY; missing variables cause exit.
getLanguages constructs an authenticated HTTPS GET to the Transifex project resource stats endpoint, reads JSON and skips English.
pullCatalog takes args[0] as the output directory and requests each reviewed PO translation over HTTPS using Basic authentication.

For each language, it removes the old <language>.po, then opens that path with O_CREATE|O_RDWR and writes the HTTP response bytes. Removal precedes writing; no overwrite-pass, random fill, raw device target or secure-erasure operation is present.
The source is unobfuscated. No hidden decoding or payload execution exists in the reviewed path.
release_diff: The relevant helper and all i18n source are unchanged. Reviewed source differences add custom library selection, platform deprecation display, serial reset callbacks, custom public-key verification, cache rebuild checks, shell quoting and CI setup-task migration. go-paths-helper changes from 1.4.0 to 1.5.0. Nested Go modules omitted by Go module ZIP packaging account for example/tool removals relative to the tag source ZIP.
changes: Replace the O_CREATE regex that stops at the first closing parenthesis with a Go AST query over the actual second OpenFile argument; keep notable severity and existing wipe-rule exclusion.
Add a notable SetBasicAuth detection requiring receiver provenance from net/http.NewRequest or NewRequestWithContext; arbitrary same-named methods and quoted calls do not match.
Keep the original source as a benign regression fixture with required file, HTTP and authentication behaviors and a forbidden wipe finding.
shared_rule_review: O_CREATE has one exact consumer, the secure-wipe-pattern exclusion. That composite feeds secure-wiper and go-disk-wiper. The new basic-auth atom has no directory consumers; existing exact Python/JS basic-auth consumers are unaffected.

verification.classifier: Calibrated BENIGN before and after (class 0, level -1); aggregate raw probability 0.8152735 -> 0.7594772. No remaining rule/verdict disagreement.
verification.existing_attack_controls: All findings unchanged across four existing Go root-checked direct-device zero-write fixtures and two archived mounted-device/MBR wipe fixtures, including their members (14 reported units).
verification.matcher_controls: Six isolated OpenFile controls passed: nested/multiline/reordered creation flags, direct creation, retained erase operation and both wipe consumers, creation text in a path, a trailing comment and quoted source. Four authentication controls passed: aliased NewRequest, NewRequestWithContext, unrelated method and quoted call.
verification.material_detection_losses: Only the unsupported secure-wipe objective is removed. The engine also prunes unreferenced baseline os.Remove text matches; every affected file retains its precise os.Remove or os.RemoveAll call detection. No accurate behavior or tested attack coverage is lost.

limits: No deployment circumstances were supplied and the sample was not executed. Existing analyzer source-flow and embedded-workflow limitations remain; provenance, direct source tracing and the release comparison support the benign judgment independently of scan scores.
